title: OpenWrt fault-injection platform
summary: A platform that breaks Wi-Fi, DHCP and DNS on demand, so flaky connectivity bugs become deterministic. One CLI command runs N devices at once across multiple fault modes.
highlights: Proposed and built it from a recurring NTP-failure pattern in QA tickets; nobody had assigned the work.
Fault profiles drive nftables/iptables rules, tc + ifb bandwidth shaping and tcpdump capture on an OpenWrt router.
Each session writes an artifact bundle: pcap, before/after firewall state and a structured pass/inconclusive summary.
Replaced one-device-at-a-time manual disconnect testing; it became the standard method for EVT/DVT, post-production and post-build validation.

details.heading: Problem
details.body: Intermittent connectivity failures on devices could not be reproduced on demand, and the manual method was to disconnect one device at a time.

details.heading: Constraint
details.body: The first prototype ran on a Raspberry Pi. Its single-radio Wi-Fi cannot run AP and STA mode at the same time. I identified that as the root cause after about two weeks.

details.heading: My part
details.body: Proposed the tool, then moved to a commercial multi-radio router reflashed with OpenWrt and delivered a working tool in under two weeks.

details.heading: Status
details.body: Professional work. The code is not public.
